title: Properties and comparison of risk capital allocation methods
abstract: If a financial unit (a bank, an insurance company, a portfolio, the financial system of a country, etc.) consists of subunits (divisions, subportfolios, etc.), then the risk of the main unit should be allocated to the subunits using a risk capital allocation method in a fair way.
summary_en: When a bank, insurance company, or financial system is composed of subunits, the total risk capital must be allocated back to those subunits in a defensible way for internal capital management and regulatory reporting. Balog, Bátyi, Csóka and Pintér survey and compare the major risk-capital-allocation methods (proportional, marginal, Aumann-Shapley, Shapley-value, etc.) on three core fairness axioms: efficiency, no-undercut (no subunit pays more than its standalone risk), and consistency. They show no method satisfies all properties simultaneously, providing a clear reference for practitioners and supervisors choosing between methods.
data_used: Theoretical comparison plus simulation analysis of risk-allocation methods applied to standardised portfolio examples. No primary firm-level dataset.
policy_relevance: Direct relevance for MNB's supervisory review of internal capital adequacy assessment processes (ICAAP) at Hungarian banks. The paper provides a clean framework for evaluating how Hungarian banks attribute risk capital across business lines — useful when MNB challenges allocations or sets ICAAP guidance. Also relevant for OTP, MKB, and other large Hungarian banks designing internal capital-allocation systems.
